auth.subtitle: Sign in to manage your library.

library.title: Library
library.emptyHint: <add>Add a movie</add> or <scan>scan an existing library</scan>.
library.loadError: The library could not be loaded.

available.label: Available
available.hint: has a file, no upgrade wanted

cutoffUnmet.label: Cutoff unmet
cutoffUnmet.hint: has a file below the profile's cutoff, an upgrade is wanted

missing.label: Missing
missing.hint: out per its minimum availability, no file yet

pending.label: Pending
pending.hint: not out yet per its minimum availability

unmonitored.label: Unmonitored
unmonitored.hint: dashed and faded, no automatic search or upgrade

sort.label: Sort by
sort.title: Title
sort.lastPlayedOf: Sort by the last play of

filter.label: Filter
filter.scopeHint: Which version monitoring, status, played, quality, tags and root folder look at.

savedViews.label: Views
savedViews.saveHint: Keeps the filters, the sort and the layout under a name, for you on this browser.
savedViews.name: Name

tagsHint.add: The picked tags are added; other tags stay.
tagsHint.remove: The picked tags are removed; other tags stay.
tagsHint.replace: The version's tags become exactly the picked ones.

bulk.noTags: No tags yet: create one below.

delete.allHint: Every version goes: the movies leave the library.
delete.versionHint: Only {{target}} of each movie goes. A movie whose last version it is leaves the library.
delete.deleteFilesHint: To the recycle bin when one is set in media management, otherwise for good.
delete.exclusionHint: For movies that leave the library: a scan or an import will not add them back.
delete.planning: Working out what would be deleted…
delete.nothing: Nothing to delete with this version choice.
delete.planFilmsRemoved_one: {{count}} movie loses its last version and leaves the library.
delete.planFilmsRemoved_other: {{count}} movies lose their last version and leave the library.
delete.planPromoted_one: {{count}} movie gets a new default version: {{names}}.
delete.planPromoted_other: {{count}} movies get a new default version: {{names}}.
delete.planNoFiles: None of these versions has a file.
delete.planFilesRecycled_one: {{count}} file goes to the recycle bin ({{path}}).
delete.planFilesRecycled_other: {{count}} files go to the recycle bin ({{path}}).
delete.planFilesDeleted_one: {{count}} file is deleted for good: no recycle bin is set.
delete.planFilesDeleted_other: {{count}} files are deleted for good: no recycle bin is set.

addMovie.noRootFolder: No film root folder yet. <link>Add one</link> before adding a movie.
addMovie.searchOnAddHint: The indexers are queried in the background once the movie is added and the best release is grabbed.

seriesLibrary.title: Series
seriesLibrary.loadError: The series could not be loaded.

addSeries.title: Add a series
addSeries.noRootFolder: No series root folder yet. <link>Add one</link> (kind “Series”) before adding a series.
addSeries.seriesTypeHint: Anime: absolute numbering. Daily: episodes named by air date.
addSeries.monitorHint: Which episodes this version wants. Specials are switched on one by one.
addSeries.noTvdb: Not on TVDB: episodes follow TMDB's order.

seriesDetail.confirmDelete: {{title}}, its versions and their monitoring leave the library. No file on disk is touched.
seriesDetail.applyMonitoringHint: Rewrites the episode and season flags of the {{version}} version. Other versions keep theirs.
seriesDetail.confirmDeleteVersion: Delete the {{version}} version? Its monitoring goes with it.
seriesDetail.lastVersion: This is the only version: deleting it deletes the series.

unmatched.hint: Video files in this version’s folder the scan could not attach to an episode. They stay where they are; rename or move them, then rescan.

seriesDetail.constraintsHint: Releases this version accepts on top of its profile. When several versions accept a release, the one with the most specific constraints gets it, then the default version.

movie.confirmDelete: Delete “{{title}}” and all its versions? Files stay on disk.
movie.confirmExclude: Also exclude this movie from future automatic additions?
movie.deleteFiles: Also delete the files from disk
movie.deleteFilesHint: The movie folder goes to the recycle bin when one is configured in Settings → Media management, otherwise it is deleted for good.

versions.title: Versions
versions.confirmDelete: Delete version “{{name}}”? The file stays on disk.
versions.noManagedCandidate: No other managed version can become the default.
versions.name: Name
versions.modeOneShot: One shot: downloaded once, never upgraded
versions.confirmDeleteFile: Delete the file of version “{{name}}”? It goes to the recycle bin when one is configured, and the version becomes missing again.

settings.versionsHint: Film or series versions stored in this folder, with or without files yet. A folder can't be removed while any point at it.
settings.removeFailed: The root folder could not be removed.
settings.addFailed: The root folder could not be added.
settings.scanHint: The scan is read-only. In a film root, one top-level folder is one movie and one video file one version, unmonitored. In a series root, one top-level folder is one series version: its files are attached to the episodes they hold, the rest is listed. Nothing is moved or renamed.

storage.title: Storage
storage.freeUnknownHint: A root folder does not report its free space, so the bar shows the space used only.
storage.open: Show the films stored here in the library, biggest first
storage.segment_one: {{path}}: {{size}} in {{count}} file, {{share}} of the space used
storage.segment_other: {{path}}: {{size}} in {{count}} files, {{share}} of the space used

settings.unmappedEmpty: None. Every scanned folder found its movie or series.
settings.unmappedHint: A film folder is imported by hand into a movie already in the library (add the movie first). A series folder is mapped to a show: one in the library gets it as a version, another one is added, unmonitored.
settings.kindLocked: Versions live here: the kind cannot change any more.

pathPicker.browseHint: The folders below are the ones Bigarr can see, on the machine it runs on.

indexers.title: Indexers
indexers.hint: Indexers added by hand speak Torznab, as Jackett's do. The mock indexer fabricates releases for any film and is meant for development.
indexers.confirmDelete: Delete “{{name}}”? History and blocklist entries keep its name.
indexers.removeFailed: The indexer could not be deleted.
indexers.empty: No indexers yet. Add one to search for releases.
indexers.name: Name
indexers.mockHint: Fabricates a realistic list of releases for whatever film you search, including a few that must be rejected. No network, no download.
indexers.urlHint: Scheme and host of the Torznab endpoint, e.g. http://prowlarr:9696/1 — the API path is added.
indexers.categoriesHint: Newznab category ids, comma separated. Defaults to every Movies category.
indexers.priorityHint: 1 is highest, 50 lowest. Breaks ties between equal releases.
indexers.rateLimitHint: Minimum delay between two requests. Failures add an escalating pause on top.
indexers.testOk: Indexer reachable: {{categories}} categories, {{releases}} recent releases, id search: {{ids}}.
indexers.prowlarrHint: Prowlarr's indexers come from Prowlarr, as in Radarr: add Bigarr there as a Radarr application (Settings → Apps → + → Radarr) and it adds, updates and removes them here on every sync.
indexers.prowlarrHowTo: URL and key to give it
indexers.prowlarrManaged: Managed by Prowlarr: every sync rewrites its name, URL, key, categories, priority, seeders, seed criteria and RSS and search switches, and deleting it in Prowlarr removes it here. Change those in Prowlarr; the rate limit is yours.
indexers.seriesCategoriesHint: What series searches and the series feed ask (anime adds its own). Left empty, they are filled from the indexer's capabilities at the first series search or test: Prowlarr only pushes movie categories to an app declared as Radarr.
indexers.testNoTv: No tv-search: series are searched by text.

search.title: Interactive search
search.hint: Queries every indexer once for this film and shows every release with how it fits each version. Type another name or spelling to search by that text instead.
search.textResults: Results for “{{query}}”, judged against this film's versions. A release whose title does not match can still be grabbed by hand.
search.fitSort: Best first: matched, accepted, then quality, score, indexer priority and seeders
search.grabHint: The grab button sends the release to the download client for the version it names: the one that accepts it, or the closest. The arrow next to it picks another version or a new one-shot version; a rejected release can still be grabbed on purpose.
search.grabAnyway: Grab for {{version}} anyway (rejected for this version)
search.grabMismatch: Grab for {{version}} anyway: the title does not match this film
search.grabBlocked: This version already has an active download
search.picked: Shadow mode: “{{title}}” recorded as Bigarr's pick for {{version}}; nothing was sent to a download client.
search.autoSearchHint: Search the indexers and grab the best release for this version
search.autoNoIndexer: {{label}}: no indexer has automatic search enabled.

rss.title: Releases
rss.hint: Every release in the RSS feeds is matched to the library and judged by each version of the film, again at every pass while the feed carries it. The first pass runs a minute after startup.
rss.hintManual: Every release in the RSS feeds is matched to the library and judged by each version of the film, again at every pass while the feed carries it. No pass runs on its own: click Sync now.
rss.schedulerOff: Automatic RSS sync off (scheduler disabled): a pass runs when you click Sync now
rss.synced: RSS pass done: {{fetched}} releases, {{new}} new, {{matched}} matched, {{grabbed}} grabbed.
rss.syncedShadow: RSS pass done: {{fetched}} releases, {{new}} new, {{matched}} matched, {{picked}} picked (shadow mode).
rss.emptyMatched: No release matched a film of the library yet.
rss.pickedHint: Shadow mode: this is what Bigarr would have grabbed. It is recorded for Activity → Compare and nothing was sent to a download client.
rss.grabHint: Each pass sends the best attributed release of every version to a download client. A release attributed but not grabbed lost to a better one of the same pass, or was refused by the client.

quality.title: Quality
quality.profilesHint: A profile ranks qualities (the order is the rank), sets the cutoff where a version is complete, and scores custom formats. A version follows one profile.
quality.name: Name
quality.languageHint: ISO 639-1 code (en, fr…). Bazarr reads it.
quality.cutoffHint: Quality at which a version is complete; above it nothing is fetched unless the custom format score is below the cutoff score.
quality.upgradeAllowed: Upgrade a file when a better release appears
quality.minFormatScoreHint: Releases scoring below are never wanted.
quality.cutoffFormatScoreHint: With the quality cutoff met and this score reached, nothing more is fetched.
quality.minUpgradeFormatScore: Minimum score gain for an upgrade
quality.minUpgradeFormatScoreHint: At equal quality a release must gain at least this much to replace the file.
quality.qualitiesHint: Best at the top. Ticked qualities are wanted; grouped ones rank together.
quality.formatScoresHint: Zero means the format is ignored by this profile. Formats are created or imported in Settings → Custom formats.
quality.confirmDelete: Delete “{{name}}”? Versions using it must be moved first.
quality.definitionsHint: Sizes in MB per minute of runtime. A release outside the range is rejected; leave max empty for no limit.
quality.saveFailed: The change could not be saved.
quality.kindHint: Film versions take Films or Both profiles, series versions Series or Both. The Radarr follow only writes Films profiles, the Sonarr follow only Series ones.
quality.kindInUse: Used by {{films}} film version(s) and {{series}} series version(s): a kind that excludes them is refused until they move.
quality.seriesDefinitionsHint: Series sizes, in MB per minute of every episode a release covers, apart from the films'. They start from Sonarr's defaults, and the Sonarr import and follow keep them in line with Sonarr's.

customFormats.title: Custom formats
customFormats.hint: A custom format recognises a trait of a release: a group, a codec, HDR, a language, a size… Each quality profile gives it a score, positive to prefer, negative to avoid. Build one by hand or paste JSON.
customFormats.importHint: Paste a Radarr export or guide files (TRaSH and the like), one format or an array. A format already present, same guide id or else same name, is updated. Scores are left for you to set.
customFormats.testFailed: The title could not be evaluated.
customFormats.noneMatched: No custom format matches this title.
customFormats.testLanguageHint: The film’s original language (ISO code): a release naming no language is assumed to speak it.
customFormats.name: Name
customFormats.applySuggested: Apply the score the guide file suggests, {{score}}
customFormats.scoreFailed: The score could not be saved.
customFormats.confirmDelete: Delete “{{name}}”? Profile scores and version constraints referring to it are removed.
customFormats.deleteFailed: The custom format could not be deleted.
customFormats.empty: No custom formats yet. Create one, or import JSON from a Radarr export or a guide.
customFormats.thresholdsHint: Minimum score, cutoff score and upgrade gain are set on each quality profile.

editor.name: Name
editor.includeWhenRenaming: Use this format in file names
editor.conditionsHint: Conditions of the same type: one must match. Conditions of different types: all must match. A required condition must always match.
editor.scoresHint: One score per quality profile. Zero: the profile ignores this format.
editor.jsonHint: Radarr’s shape: what you write here can go to Radarr and back.
editor.jsonInvalid: This JSON is not a custom format: {{message}}

downloadClients.title: Download clients
downloadClients.hint: Grabs are sent to the enabled client with the lowest priority number. Every torrent Bigarr adds carries the category below; the queue is what the client holds in that category. Downloads and libraries must share one mount for imports to hardlink.
downloadClients.confirmDelete: Delete “{{name}}”? Its downloads stay in the client; Bigarr stops following them.
downloadClients.removeFailed: The download client could not be deleted.
downloadClients.empty: No download client yet. Add one to grab releases.
downloadClients.name: Name
downloadClients.mockHint: Downloads complete on their own after a minute and a half, without any network. Meant to exercise the queue.
downloadClients.hostHint: Host name or address of the WebUI, without scheme or port.
downloadClients.passwordHint: Leave both empty when the WebUI has authentication disabled for this address.
downloadClients.categoryHint: Created in qBittorrent if missing. Keep one category per Bigarr instance.
downloadClients.seriesCategoryHint: Series grabs go here (Sonarr uses tv-sonarr). Must differ from the film category: it tells a finished download holds episodes.
downloadClients.priorityHint: 1 is tried first when several clients are enabled.

queue.title: Queue
queue.liveHint: Connected to the server stream: the table updates after every poll of the download clients.
queue.pollingHint: The stream is down; the table refreshes every 10 seconds instead.
queue.noClients: No download client is enabled. Add one in Settings → Download clients.
queue.removeFailed: The download could not be removed.
queue.removeFromClient: Also remove the torrent from the download client
queue.removeFromClientHint: Unchecked, the torrent keeps running in the client and Bigarr just stops following it.
queue.deleteFilesHint: What the client has written so far. Nothing in the library is touched.
queue.blocklistHint: The release is refused for this version from now on. Use it for a fake or a broken torrent, not for a slow one.
queue.retryImportFailed: The import could not be retried.

rename.title: Rename files
rename.hint: Applies the current file name template of Settings → Media management to the files of this movie and to the extra files imported with them. Nothing else moves.
rename.nothing: Every file already matches the template.

history.title: History
history.loadError: The history could not be loaded.

manualImport.title: Manual import
manualImport.hint: Pick the movie and the version for each file. The import is forced: no upgrade check, an existing file is replaced through the recycle bin.
manualImport.loadFailed: The path could not be read.
manualImport.empty: No video file found under this path.
manualImport.noMovieHint: Add the movie to the library first, then pick it here.

seriesFiles.renameHint: The files of this version renamed to the current episode naming (Settings → Media management). The series folder never moves.
seriesFiles.nothingToRename: Every file already has its name.
seriesFiles.deleteHint: {{path}} goes to the recycle bin (or is deleted when none is set), its subtitles with it. The episode becomes missing.
seriesFiles.deleteMulti: {{path}} holds {{episodes}}: every one of them becomes missing. The file goes to the recycle bin, its subtitles with it.
seriesFiles.deleteSeriesFilesHint: Every folder of the series goes to the recycle bin (or is deleted when none is set).
seriesFiles.deleteVersionFilesHint: The version's files go to the recycle bin; its folder too when no other version shares it.
seriesFiles.assignRename: Rename it to the episode naming
seriesFiles.assignRenameHint: Unchecked, the file stays exactly where and how it is.
seriesFiles.assignReplaceHint: An episode that has a file is refused unless checked; the old file then goes to the recycle bin.

seriesImport.title: Manual import (series)
seriesImport.hint: Pick the series, the version and the episodes of each file. The import is forced: no upgrade check, a file in place is replaced through the recycle bin.

oneShot.title: Grab as a one-shot version
oneShot.hint: Creates a version that is grabbed once and never upgraded, next to the existing ones (a Director's Cut, a specific encode), then sends this release to the download client for it.
oneShot.name: Version name
oneShot.nameHint: A short slug: directors-cut, imax, remux-framestor…
oneShot.editionHint: Prefilled from the release; only releases matching it count for this version later.
oneShot.rolledBack: The version was removed again because the grab failed.

seriesNaming.title: Episode naming
seriesNaming.hint: Sonarr's naming for series: the tokens and multi-episode styles are Sonarr's, the defaults too. New series and new versions take the series folder template; existing folders never move on their own. Rename a series from its page to apply new templates to its files.
seriesNaming.renameEpisodesHint: Off: imported episodes keep their download name (still sorted into season folders).
seriesNaming.seriesFolderHint: Applied when a series or a version is added; the folder name is then frozen.
seriesNaming.tokensHint: Click a token to add it to the {{field}}. Grey tokens also work in folder names.

mediaManagement.title: Media management
mediaManagement.hint: How finished downloads reach the library: file naming, transfer mode and the recycle bin that receives replaced or deleted files.
mediaManagement.renameFilesHint: Off: files keep the name they had in the download. Existing files can be renamed later from each movie page.
mediaManagement.folderTemplateHint: Applied when a version is created; the folder name is then frozen so files never move silently.
mediaManagement.tokensHint: Radarr syntax: anything between the braces around a token is printed only when the token has a value, so {(Release Year)} disappears without a year. Lower-case tokens print in lower case, {Movie.Title} joins words with dots. {Version} is the version name.
mediaManagement.transferModeHint: A hardlink puts the same bytes under two names: the torrent keeps seeding for free. It needs downloads and the library on one filesystem, at the same path for the client and for Bigarr. Move only makes sense once seeding is over.
mediaManagement.recycleBinPathHint: Replaced and deleted files land here, keeping their path relative to the root folder. Empty: they are deleted for good.
mediaManagement.retentionHint: Files older than this are removed from the bin every hour. 0 keeps them until you empty it yourself.
mediaManagement.retentionHintManual: Files older than this are removed from the bin when the maintenance task runs, by hand while the scheduler is off (System → Status). 0 keeps them until you empty it yourself.
mediaManagement.importExtraFilesHint: Subtitles and other side files of the release come along with the movie, with the same transfer, named after the movie file with their language. They follow its renames and leave with it on an upgrade or a deletion. Files Bigarr did not import, such as Bazarr's subtitles, are never renamed nor deleted.
mediaManagement.extraFileExtensionsHint: Comma separated, without dots: srt,ass,ssa,sub,idx,sup,vtt. Other extensions (nfo, pdf…) come along under the movie's name; a release's .nfo is kept as .nfo-orig, once, so media servers do not read it as metadata. Video extensions are refused.
mediaManagement.mediaInfoAvailable: ffprobe found at {{path}}: imported files get their codecs, channels, HDR and languages read from the stream.
mediaManagement.mediaInfoMissing: ffprobe was not found: files are imported without media info. Install ffmpeg (the Docker image ships it) or set Bigarr__Media__FfprobePath.
mediaManagement.saveFailed: The settings could not be saved.
mediaManagement.seasonPackUpgradeHint: When a season pack counts as an upgrade over the episode files it would replace, as in Sonarr. Episodes without a file always count as upgraded. “Any one episode” may replace better files with worse ones.

wanted.title: Wanted
wanted.hint: Monitored versions without a file, and files below their profile cutoff. The cutoff-unmet task searches them on its own, waiting longer after each empty search; a search from here ignores that wait.
wanted.hintManual: Monitored versions without a file, and files below their profile cutoff. The scheduler is off, so nothing searches them on its own: search from here, or run the cutoff-unmet task from System → Status.
wanted.empty: Nothing is wanted: every monitored version has its file at the cutoff.
wanted.nextSearchHint: When the cutoff-unmet task may search this version again. The wait doubles after each empty search.

blocklist.title: Blocklist
blocklist.hint: Releases refused for a version: failed downloads land here on their own, removals from the queue when you ask. Dropping an entry lets the release be grabbed again.
blocklist.removeFailed: The entry could not be removed.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.hint: Webhooks: every event Bigarr publishes is POSTed to each endpoint that subscribes to it, as Bigarr's JSON, Radarr's, or a Discord message, for every film or only tagged ones, signed with the secret when there is one, and retried until it lands, restarts included.
notifications.name: Name
notifications.secretHint: Optional. When set, X-Bigarr-Signature carries an HMAC-SHA256 of the body so the receiver can check the origin.
notifications.secretKeepHint: This endpoint is signed. Leave empty to remove the secret, or type a new one.
notifications.allEventsHint: Nothing checked: every event is sent.
notifications.testOk: The endpoint answered HTTP {{status}} in {{ms}} ms.
notifications.testFailed: The endpoint did not accept the test event.
notifications.confirmDelete: Delete “{{name}}”? Its pending deliveries are dropped.
notifications.removeFailed: The webhook could not be deleted.
notifications.formatBigarrHint: Bigarr's own JSON, { eventType, eventId, occurredAt, instance, data }, with the full snapshot of the film, version, release and file.
notifications.formatRadarrHint: The body Radarr's webhook sends, so tools written for Radarr (Notifiarr, autoscan, autopulse, a Discord bot that reads Radarr webhooks…) work unchanged. A Discord channel webhook URL cannot read it: use the Discord format for that. A Radarr movie is a version: its id is the one /api/v3/movie gives an API key of the same view.
notifications.formatDiscordHint: Messages for a Discord channel webhook (channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → Copy Webhook URL), laid out like Radarr's Discord connection: the film and its version, quality, release, links and poster. The URL holds the webhook's token: keep it private.
notifications.discordUrlDetected: This is a Discord webhook URL. Discord only reads its own messages, not this format.
notifications.discordUsernameHint: Overrides the name the webhook posts under.
notifications.discordAuthorHint: Shown above each message; Bigarr when empty.
notifications.discordAvatarHint: Overrides the webhook's avatar: an image URL.
notifications.discordFieldsHint: What each message carries, as in Radarr's Discord connection. The poster is the thumbnail, the fanart the large image; empty values are left out.
notifications.discordImportFields: On import and upgrade (poster and fanart also on added and deleted films)
notifications.viewVersionHint: Only this version of each film is sent; films without it stay silent. View:
notifications.allFilmsHint: Nothing checked: every film is sent.
notifications.someTagsHint: Only films whose versions carry one of the checked tags. Health and test events are always sent.
notifications.noTags: No tag yet. Tags come with Seerr requests and the Radarr import.
notifications.radarrEventsHint: Radarr's format only sends the events Radarr has; the others are greyed out.
notifications.discordEventsHint: Discord gets what Radarr's Discord connection posts, plus failed downloads and imports and versions added, deleted or made the default; a version's settings changing is greyed out.

health.title: Health
health.allGood: All good: nothing stands in the way of the loop.

tasks.title: Scheduled tasks
tasks.hint: What runs on its own: the RSS pass, the search for missing and upgradable versions, the health check, the maintenance, the weekly backup. Each can be run now.
tasks.schedulerOff: The scheduler is off (Bigarr__Scheduler__Enabled=false): no task runs on its own. Each runs only when triggered, here with Run now or from its own page.

connect.title: Connect
connect.hint: Bigarr speaks Radarr v3 on /api/v3, so Seerr, Bazarr and Prowlarr plug in as if it were a Radarr. Each connected app gets its own key, and the key decides which version of each film it sees.
connect.name: Name
connect.viewDefault: Default version of each film (a classic Radarr)
connect.viewAll: Every version, one line each (for Bazarr)
connect.viewVersion: One named version only (a Seerr entry for 4K)
connect.versionNameHint: A lowercase slug. Adding a film through this key creates a version of this name; films without it stay invisible to the key.
connect.created: Key created. Copy it now: it is shown only once.
connect.copyFailed: Could not copy; select the text and copy it by hand.
connect.confirmRevoke: Revoke “{{name}}”? The app using it loses access immediately; the key cannot be restored.
connect.noKeys: No key yet. Create one per app you connect.
connect.createFailed: The key could not be created.
connect.revokeFailed: The key could not be revoked.
connect.url: Radarr URL to enter in the app
connect.seerrHint: One Seerr, two Radarr servers on this same URL: a standard server with a version:1080p key and a 4K server with a version:4k key. Each request creates or follows its own version of the film; both servers can share the root folder. Pick the matching quality profile on each.
connect.bazarrHint: One Bazarr per version, like the usual Bazarr + Bazarr 4K pair: a version:1080p key on the first, a version:4k key on the second. Bazarr keeps one line per TMDB id, so a key with the all view would make it skip the second version of a film. Each instance follows its files live over SignalR at /signalr/messages.
connect.prowlarrHint: In Prowlarr, Settings → Apps → + → Radarr: Prowlarr Server is Prowlarr's URL as Bigarr reaches it, Radarr Server is the URL above, API Key a key with the default view, sync level Full Sync. Prowlarr then pushes its torrent indexers here and keeps them in sync.

backups.title: Backups
backups.hint: A zip of the database, taken every week and kept four weeks (Bigarr__Backup__IntervalDays, RetentionDays). Restoring stages the file and restarts Bigarr; in Docker the container comes back on the restored database.
backups.hintManual: A zip of the database. The scheduler is off, so no weekly backup is taken and old ones are not pruned: click Back up now, or run the Backup task above. Restoring stages the file and restarts Bigarr; in Docker the container comes back on the restored database.
backups.createFailed: The backup could not be written.
backups.name: Backup
backups.confirmRestore: Restore “{{name}}”? Everything added since it was taken is lost. Bigarr restarts right away with the restored database; the current one is kept next to it as bigarr.db.before-restore.
backups.restoring: Bigarr is restarting on the restored database. Reload this page in a few seconds.
backups.restoreFailed: The backup could not be restored.
backups.removeFailed: The backup could not be deleted.

compare.title: Compare with Radarr
compare.intro: Shadow mode, film by film: what the followed Radarr grabbed next to what Bigarr would have grabbed for the same version, paired by release (guid, info hash, title), else by film and version within the window. Open a row to see why each side chose what it did.
compare.windowHint: How far apart a grab and a pick of the same film and version can be and still be compared. Picks made while Radarr's download was in flight stay with its grab.

outcomeHints.different: Both chose, not the same release

compare.agreement: Bigarr picked the same release for {{percent}}% of Radarr's grabs ({{same}} of {{grabs}}).
compare.noGrabs: No Radarr grab in this period yet.
compare.empty: Nothing to compare yet: Bigarr's picks come from its RSS passes, Radarr's grabs from the followed Radarrs' history.
compare.shadowOffHint: Bigarr grabs for real, so it records no pick to compare: set Bigarr__Shadow__Enabled=true to run it next to Radarr.
compare.noRadarrHint: Radarr's grabs come from the Radarrs Bigarr follows:
compare.filmHint: What the followed Radarrs grabbed for this film next to what Bigarr would have grabbed, all time. Activity → Compare has every film.
compare.alsoPicked_one: Bigarr also picked {{count}} release while Radarr's download was in flight
compare.alsoPicked_other: Bigarr also picked {{count}} releases while Radarr's download was in flight
compare.differentHint: A pick changes nothing in Bigarr: until Radarr's file lands, Bigarr keeps judging the version as wanted.
compare.fileThen: The version had {{quality}} (score {{score}}) when Radarr grabbed.
compare.pickThen: Bigarr had already picked {{quality}} (score {{score}}) when Radarr grabbed: judged against that pick, the file Bigarr would have had.
compare.noFileThen: The version had no file when Radarr grabbed.
compare.notAskedYet: Not shown to Radarr yet: the next pass of the follow asks it.
compare.radarrNoFilm: Radarr does not match this title to any of its films.
compare.radarrOtherFilm: Radarr matches this title to another film.
compare.radarrUnmonitored: The film is unmonitored in Radarr.

radarrFollow.title: Followed Radarrs
radarrFollow.intro: The Radarrs Bigarr runs next to before replacing them. Each one is a version of your films: Bigarr reads its history (what it grabbed, imported, upgraded) and keeps that version in line with its library, so what Bigarr would grab can be compared with what Radarr grabs. Bigarr only reads from Radarr.
radarrFollow.dialogHint: Same mapping as the import: each Radarr profile and root folder to Bigarr's. Films added to Radarr later come in with it, and each mapped Bigarr profile keeps the qualities, cutoff and scores of its Radarr profile on every pass.
radarrFollow.name: Name
radarrFollow.versionHint: The version this Radarr's films are in Bigarr: 1080p, 4k…
radarrFollow.confirmDelete: {{name}} will no longer be read. Its grabs leave the comparison; Bigarr's picks and the films it brought in stay.
radarrFollow.empty: No Radarr is followed yet. Follow one here, or tick “Keep following this Radarr” at the end of an import:
radarrFollow.readOnlyHint: Bigarr only sends GET requests to Radarr and never writes to disk for it: a file Radarr imports is recorded in Bigarr's database as the version's file, if Bigarr can see it through the mapped root folder.
radarrFollow.keyHintSaved: Leave it untouched to keep the stored key; it is never sent back to the browser.
radarrFollow.mappingHint: Load Radarr's profiles and root folders to map them to Bigarr's.
radarrFollow.enabledHint: Paused, nothing is read; the checkpoint stays, so the next pass catches up.
radarrFollow.webhookHint: In Radarr: Settings → Connect → + → Webhook, method POST, this URL with Bigarr's address as Radarr reaches it and a Bigarr API key in place of YOUR_API_KEY. Tick On Movie Added, On Grab, On File Import, On File Upgrade, On Rename and On Movie File Delete. Each event then reads Radarr within seconds, instead of at the next scheduled pass, which keeps running anyway. API keys:
radarrFollow.webhookAfterSave: Save first: the webhook's URL names this Radarr.
radarrFollow.shadowOnHint: Bigarr records what it would grab ({{picks}} picks so far) and sends nothing to a download client; {{grabs}} Radarr grabs read so far.
radarrFollow.shadowOffHint: Bigarr grabs for real. Following a Radarr is meant for shadow mode, next to it: set Bigarr__Shadow__Enabled=true so Bigarr records its picks instead.

importRadarr.title: Import from Radarr
importRadarr.intro: Moves a Radarr library into Bigarr. Each Radarr movie becomes one version of the film, with its monitored flag, quality profile, tags, minimum availability and file. Metadata comes from Radarr itself, so there is no TMDB round trip. The library folders must be reachable from Bigarr under a mapped root folder.
importRadarr.urlHint: Scheme, host and port, with any URL base, e.g. http://radarr:7878.
importRadarr.summary: Radarr {{version}}: {{movies}} movies, {{withFile}} with a file, {{monitored}} monitored, {{already}} already in this library, {{exclusions}} exclusions, {{history}} history lines, {{blocklist}} blocklisted releases, {{customFormats}} custom formats.
importRadarr.versionNameHint: 1080p for a standard Radarr, 4k for a 4K one. A second Radarr imported with another name adds versions to the same films; a film that already has a version with this name gets Radarr's settings instead of a new version.
importRadarr.versionNameInvalid: A version name is a lowercase slug: letters, digits and single dashes.
importRadarr.rootFoldersHint: The Radarr path is read as is on this host when it is reachable; otherwise pick the root folder where the same films live, added on the Library settings page.
importRadarr.noTags: Radarr has no tags in use.
importRadarr.importCustomFormats: Import custom formats and give each mapped profile the scores of its Radarr profile
importRadarr.importProfileQualities: Give each mapped profile the qualities of its Radarr profile: which are allowed, their order and groups, the cutoff, upgrades
importRadarr.importHistory: Import history (grabs, imports, failures, deletions, renames of the imported films)
importRadarr.importBlocklist: Import blocklist (releases Radarr rejected for the imported films are not grabbed again)
importRadarr.follow: Keep following this Radarr afterwards (shadow mode)
importRadarr.followHint: Bigarr then reads this Radarr's history and library every few minutes with the same mapping: its grabs feed Activity → Compare, and the films and files it adds land in this version. Settings → Followed Radarrs.
importRadarr.mappingIncomplete: Map every profile and root folder that has movies, and give a valid version name.

importTautulli.title: Import from Tautulli
importTautulli.intro: Brings Tautulli's play history into Bigarr: its users, every film and episode play with its streams, and the film and version each play was of. Run it as often as you like: plays already imported are skipped, and a play Bigarr followed live wins over the same play in Tautulli.
importTautulli.serverHint: The Plex server Tautulli watches: its users and plays get the history.
importTautulli.noPlex: Add the Plex server Tautulli watches first, in
importTautulli.pathHint: A copy of tautulli.db on the Bigarr host: one of Tautulli's own backups (backups/tautulli.backup-….db), or tautulli.db copied while Tautulli is stopped. The file is only read.
importTautulli.uploaded: Uploaded ({{size}}). The copy is deleted once the import is done.
importTautulli.uploadHint: Or send the file from this computer: it is kept in Bigarr's config folder until the import is done.
importTautulli.previewFailed: The database could not be read.
importTautulli.filmsHint: A play is linked by the film's TMDB or IMDb id, else by its title and year. Its version comes from the Plex library it was played from, else from the only version with a file or the played resolution. Unmatched plays are kept under their title.
importTautulli.askPlexHint: Films Tautulli only knows by a Plex guid get their ids from Plex while it still has them, and every show its current title and ids. Off: films are linked by title and year only, shows keep Tautulli’s title.
importTautulli.noIssues: Every film play was linked to a film.
importTautulli.issuesHint: Their plays are kept under Tautulli’s title. The Plays page lists them any time under “Films not linked”.

importSonarr.title: Import from Sonarr
importSonarr.intro: Moves a Sonarr library into Bigarr. Each Sonarr series becomes one version of the show, matched on its TVDB id, with its monitoring (series, seasons, episodes), quality profile, tags, season folders and episode files; a file holding several episodes is recorded once. Seasons, episodes and metadata come from Sonarr itself, so there is no TVDB round trip; the show is refreshed later. Nothing on disk is touched.

A Sonarr format Bigarr already has under the same name and definition is reused; the same name with another definition comes in as “name (Sonarr)”; any other is created. Their scores only go to the Series profiles of this import. Indexer flags, languages and sources are translated to Bigarr's numbering; a specification Bigarr cannot evaluate is kept, marked and listed.
